# VIETNAM THERMAL POWER GENERATION INVENTORY (>30 MWe)

**Compiled:** May 2026 | **Analyst:** Energy Sector Research | **Classification:** Primary-sourced inventory

---

## 1. Sector Overview

Vietnam's electricity system has undergone rapid expansion, growing from ~48 GW installed capacity in 2019 to over 80 GW by 2024, driven by a surge in renewables alongside continued thermal baseload investment. Thermal power — coal, gas, and emerging LNG — remains the backbone of dispatchable generation, accounting for roughly 50–55% of total electricity output.

**Policy Framework.** The National Power Development Plan VIII (PDP8), approved under Decision 500/QĐ-TTg on 15 May 2023, sets Vietnam's generation roadmap through 2030 with a vision to 2050. The Implementation Plan (Decision 262/QĐ-TTg, 1 April 2024) and the Amended PDP8 (Decision 768/QĐ-TTg, 15 April 2025) refined targets. PDP8 caps coal at ~30,127 MW by 2030 (no new coal after 2030), targets ~22,400–22,524 MW of LNG, and envisions ~14,930 MW of domestic gas-fired capacity. A co-generation/waste-heat/blast-furnace-gas tranche of 2,700 MW is also included.

**Key Actors.** The Ministry of Industry and Trade (MOIT) oversees planning. Electricity of Vietnam (EVN) and its generation subsidiaries (EVNGENCO1, EVNGENCO2, EVNGENCO3) own the majority of utility-scale thermal assets. PetroVietnam (PVN), through PV Power, operates major gas-fired and LNG plants. The coal mining conglomerate TKV (Vinacomin) operates several mine-mouth coal plants. Private and BOT investors — including consortia led by Marubeni, KEPCO, Sumitomo, Mitsubishi, AES, Jaks Resources, and Janakuasa — hold significant stakes in coal BOT projects.

**Challenges.** Vietnam faces a complex energy trilemma: (1) phasing down coal under its Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP) commitments while demand grows 8–10% annually; (2) a stalled LNG transition — of 13 planned LNG projects (~22.4 GW), only Nhơn Trạch 3&4 (1.6 GW) have reached COD; and (3) grid integration of ~21 GW of solar/wind already installed. Long Phú 1, delayed since 2019 due to Russian sanctions on EPC contractor Power Machines, exemplifies construction risk. Five coal projects totalling ~8 GW have been cancelled or shelved (Công Thanh, Nam Định I, Quảng Trị, Vĩnh Tân 3, Sông Hậu 2).

---

## 2. Per-Plant Narratives — Major/Disputed Assets

### Vĩnh Tân Complex (Bình Thuận)
Four co-located coal plants totalling ~4,244 MW nameplate. Vĩnh Tân 2 (1,244 MW, EVNGENCO3, COD 2014–15) and Vĩnh Tân 4 + 4MR (1,800 MW combined, EVNGENCO3, COD 2017–19) are the utility-owned assets. Vĩnh Tân 1 (1,200 MW) is a BOT plant. Vĩnh Tân 3 (~1,980 MW, proposed by One Energy/CLP) was cancelled after the developer withdrew; PDP8 does not list it among plants to be built.

### Thái Bình 2 (Thái Bình)
A 1,200 MW (2×600 MW) supercritical plant developed by PVN/PV Power. The project was plagued by corruption scandals and cost overruns (originally ~$1.3B, final cost reportedly higher). It achieved commercial operation of both units in 2022–23 after a decade of construction. Now an operating asset contributing ~7 billion kWh/year.

### Long Phú 1 (Sóc Trăng)

### Ô Môn LNG Complex (Cần Thơ)
Ô Môn I (660 MW, gas CCGT) is operating under EVNGENCO2. The complex is planned to expand with three LNG-fired units — Ô Môn II, III, and IV (~1,050 MW each) — fed by LNG from the Thị Vải terminal via pipeline. Ô Môn II has JICA financing support. Gas supply agreements remain a critical bottleneck; all three LNG units are still in planning stage.

### Sơn Mỹ LNG (Bình Thuận)
A mega-project envisioning two 2,250 MW LNG-fired plants (Sơn Mỹ I and II) fed by a dedicated LNG receiving terminal. Multiple international consortia have expressed interest but neither project has reached financial close. Classified as planned; the terminal and power plants face land acquisition and gas pricing challenges.

### Nhơn Trạch 3 & 4 — Vietnam's First LNG Plants (Đồng Nai)
PV Power's Nhơn Trạch 3 and 4, each 812 MW CCGT, became Vietnam's first LNG-fired power plants to achieve commercial operation in 2025. Combined capacity of 1,624 MW. They receive regasified LNG from the Thị Vải terminal. These plants are a critical proof-of-concept for Vietnam's LNG transition.

### Vũng Áng 2 (Hà Tĩnh)
A 1,200 MW (2×600 MW) USC coal BOT project developed by a consortium of Mitsubishi, KEPCO, and Chugoku Electric. Investment of ~$2.2 billion. Unit 1 reportedly achieved COD in July 2025 per Vietnamese press. The plant suffered storm damage to its coal warehouse in September 2025. Unit 2 status uncertain.
